texts.full_text: g Of Infinity:Explanations That Transform Our Understanding (2014), David Deutsch writes: The beginning and the end are both beyond our reach -- as is every other thing that cannot be explained by explanation or demonstrated through demonstration. We have no means of knowing what preceded, caused, initiated matter; we can only speculate about it. As for a possible future after death (and I don't know if you're religious), there's nothing in the laws and equations governing physics to support such an idea: There are not even any known processes by which life could be transferred from one body or person into another. The closest thing is DNA replication, but this doesn' t involve a transfer of consciousness. But what we do have at our disposal -- that can make us feel better about ourselves and the world aroundus--is science; it allows for rational explanation to help guide decision-making processes in life's challenges As an aside: In his book The Beginning Of Infinity, David Deutsch writes: It is true also of human beings. texts.full_text: e still retaining elements of who he was as an individual artist – which makes sense given everything else we know about him from other sources such David Bowie: The Last five Years is a 2016 British television documentary series presented and produced by Francis Whately, chronicling the final five years in David’s life. It aired on BBC Two between November & December of that year with two parts released each night for four nights running – totalling eight episodes over seven days (the last episode was shown as part 2). The first three hours focused solely upon his work during these times whilst later ones looked back at earlier periods too including early childhood through to teenage years right up until just before he died aged sixty-nine in January from cancer. The documentary follows Bowie’s life and career over the course of five days, showing how David was able “to keep reinventing himself” throughout much longer than other artists would have been expected or even thought possible. It explores what made him famous originally as well; exploring new ideas within his chosen medium(s), but also retaining elements from past work that make up part who he is/was now today – making sense given everything else we know about David through various sources such music videos etcetera! But listen: just beyond this lection we find Jesus being full of the joy of the Holy Spirit as he rejoices in the grace of God that has revealed his truth to the disciples and to so many others. Soon after that he tells everybody’s favorite parable of the Good Samaritan. But the point is that you cannot understand the joy of Jesus in Luke 10:21ff and you cannot understand Jesus’ perspective in the subsequent parable that everybody is your neighbor who deserves love and ministry unless you also understand that for Jesus the joy is deepened and the need to reach out to neighbors in love is heightened precisely because he’s not talking about a game of tidily-winks here.
